week_in_history.narrative:
This week's flashback comes from 2024, Week 5 — the game that pushed Brian Kleinhenz to a flawless 5-0 start, a record that makes casual fans assume someone finally built a juggernaut instead of just a guy who got hot for a month and a half. Digger Stump put up 108.22 and buried Hawk Tua Tagoviloa's 98.34, sending Jason Carlton home to towel off a loss that stung but didn't sink him.

And it didn't — Carlton rattled off a 6-3 finish, snuck into the playoffs, and lasted right up until the quarterfinal before getting shown the exit, which is about the ceiling for a guy who apparently peaks in the regular season and chokes the second real stakes show up.

Kleinhenz, meanwhile, cooled off hard, stumbling to a 5-4 finish after this game — still playoff-bound, but he cashed in his undefeated mystique for a semifinal exit, proving a hot start is just a louder way of eventually losing in October.

stat_of_the_week.teams_label: In the top 6 in points but not the top 6 in the standings this year
stat_of_the_week.narrative: The historical chance of making the playoffs if you are in the top 6 in points but not in the top 6 in the standings after Week 4. Since 2023, 7 teams have been there. 3 of them made the playoffs: Carl Bruce (2023), Blake Pratt (2024), Kevin Mallon (2025).

weekly_recap.previous_weekend: Brian Kleinhenz survived the tightest game of the week, slipping past Blake Pratt 103.02 to 99.40 — a margin of 3.62 that'll have Pratt checking the box score for typos. This was their fourth all-time meeting with the series knotted at 2-2, and somehow still the most dramatic one yet, because Pratt actually led 99.40 to 87.82 heading into Monday Night Football before Kleinhenz's night closer dragged him across the finish line. Javonte Williams torched the field for 28.8 points for Kleinhenz, more than covering for a Chiefs D/ST that contributed a punchless 1.0. Pratt got 20.1 points from Dak Prescott, but Josh Downs no-showed with 3.1, and here's the kicker — Pratt had Ollie Gordon II sitting on his bench with 19.0 points, enough that one lineup swap wins this outright. Add in Pratt's career total of one championship across three complete seasons, and Meatloaf just proved he can still choke under pressure when it counts most.
weekly_recap.honorable_mention: The week's biggest blowout landed right in the finale slot, and Kevin Mallon turned in the kind of 66.88 points that makes you check if your kicker accidentally benched everyone. Jay Nelson's 111.12 points buried him by 44.24, extending Jay's all-time series lead to 3-0 in three meetings. Joe Burrow's 25.72 points carried Jay like he had somewhere better to be, while Rashee Rice's goose egg sealed Kevin's fate. Kevin's 20-minutes-a-day fitness routine clearly isn't being spent studying lineups — his career winning percentage sits at 38.9%. Jay, the league's trusted commissioner with a 60.9% career winning percentage, didn't even need to break a sweat enforcing this one.
weekly_recap.game_of_the_week: The King of The Crawfish, Josh Davis, limps into this one at 2-2, ranked 8th, averaging 102.8 points a game this season, which is basically what happens when you season a dish with good intentions and no follow-through. Across the table sits Eddie McCumiskey, undefeated at 4-0, ranked 1st, averaging 112.98 points a game, and riding an easy schedule that's inflated his win total like a Mumford and Sons encore nobody asked for — three choruses too many but the crowd keeps cheering anyway. Eddie's career numbers (two playoff trips, zero championships, a 56.5 career winning percentage) say "good, not great," but against Josh specifically he's been flawless, leading their all-time series 2-0. Eddie's playoff odds climbed from 90.9% last week to 90.9% now, rock solid. Josh's dipped to 48.8%, a coin flip with a crawfish boil smell he can't quite wash off. This figures to be more flush than fight.
